memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The people came to Moses and said, "We sinned when we spoke against the LORD and against you. Pray that the LORD will take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people. - Num 21:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Suffering brought the people to their senses. They came to Moses with words we do not often hear from them: "We sinned." There is no excuse-making, no blaming the circumstances. They name their sin plainly and ask for prayer.

This is what genuine repentance looks like. It does not merely regret the consequences; it owns the wrong. Israel had spoken against the Lord and against His servant, and now they confess it honestly. Confession is the doorway back to fellowship with God.

Notice too the tenderness of Moses. The very people who had attacked him with their words are now the people he prays for. He does not gloat or withdraw. He intercedes. In this we catch a small glimpse of a greater Intercessor, one who prays for those who wrong Him.

When you sin, do not run from God or hide in shame. Come as Israel came, honestly naming the wrong and asking for mercy. And remember that you have a Mediator far greater than Moses. Jesus lives to intercede for you, and His prayers never fail (Heb 7:25). Confession leads not to rejection but to restoration.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a sin you need to name honestly before God today?
2. Do you find it hard to say plainly, "I have sinned"?
3. Who might God be calling you to pray for, even if they have wronged you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a repentant heart that names sin honestly rather than hiding it. Thank You that Jesus intercedes for me and welcomes me back. Amen.
